title: refactor(ci): modernize lint/test/release workflows, optimize cache & parallelism
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Updated CI workflows to Node 20; consolidated lint, test, and release pipelines. Improved cache key strategy and parallelism to reduce overall runtime and redundant runs.
description:
Motivation: Our CI has accumulated many overlapping workflows that cause longer queue times, redundant matrix runs, and fragile caches. This PR modernizes the GitHub Actions pipelines: consolidates lint and test flows, consolidates release automation, pins action versions, upgrades runners to Node 20 where applicable, and improves cache hit rates and parallelism heuristics.

What I changed (summary):
- Consolidated separate lint.yml and test.yml into .github/workflows/lint-and-test.yml with job-level matrices to avoid duplicated checkout/build steps.
- Reworked release automation to use a single release.yml with a controlled manual trigger for stable releases and an automatic canary channel for pre-releases.
- Upgraded Node tool usage to node-version: 20 for JS/TS projects and updated relevant Action versions (actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4 pinned).
- Improved caching: unified cache key scheme using repo, job, node-version, and package-lock fingerprint; added restore-keys to improve hit rates for branch builds.
- Reduced unnecessary matrix dimensions: Windows moved to a fast-smoke OS matrix only for platform-specific tests; Linux macOS run main coverage and integration.
- Tuned parallelism and concurrency: limited max-parallel to reduce CI queue pressure and added job-level group concurrency for PRs to avoid duplicate runs on rapid pushes.
- Added small CI helper scripts and a composite action (actions/ci-helpers) to centralize cache logic and retry semantics for flaky steps.
- Fixed a flaky integration test by adding rate-limit handling and a deterministic wait helper.

Checklist:
- [x] Consolidate workflows and remove duplication
- [x] Pin GH Actions versions where appropriate
- [x] Upgrade Node to 20 in CI (non-breaking for runtime)
- [x] Improve cache keys and restore semantics
- [x] Limit matrix size and tune parallelism
- [x] Update README CI documentation

Impact and rollout notes:
- Expected CI wall-clock reduction of ~30% on common PRs due to fewer duplicated steps and better cache utilization.
- No code changes to production artifacts; this is infra-only and non-breaking.
- Release workflow change requires team awareness: stable releases now need manual confirmation; canary releases continue to run automatically for main branch builds.

Related Linear tickets: ENG-4321 (CI consolidation), ENG-4398 (CI cache improvements).

Second run: unit tests passed, integration flake observed (intermittent). Added retry and deterministic wait.

Total CI time reduced ~28% on merged PR compared to baseline (measured across three sample PRs).
motivation: Reduce CI runtime, decrease flakiness, and centralize cross-repo CI hygiene to make developer feedback faster and CI billing more efficient.
